description: 45 SaaS company logos explained by a brand designer, from Asana, HubSpot, and GitHub to Ramp, Vanta, Cursor, and ElevenLabs.
intro:
A SaaS logo spends most of its life as a favicon, an app icon, a login screen, and a Slack integration tile, so the best ones are simple enough to read at 16 pixels and distinctive enough to stand out in a crowded tool stack.

If you’re planning your own launch or rebrand, see my SaaS branding service for scope, pricing, and the Elevate case study.

What makes a good SaaS logo?

A symbol that works as an icon: buyers meet your logo inside other tools (integrations, browser tabs, dock icons), so a compact mark like the Asana dots or the Zapier underscore does a lot of work.

Color with a job: HubSpot orange, Twilio red, and Supabase green make the product recognizable in a sidebar full of other apps.

Friendly but credible type: SaaS brands sell to teams and to finance departments at the same time, so most wordmarks balance a rounded, approachable feel with clean, trustworthy proportions.

Below are 45 SaaS logos in five groups, from productivity tools to AI SaaS. Each one has a slide with my handwritten notes, followed by a short explanation.

logoResearch.name: Asana
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Asana is a work management platform used by teams to plan and track projects.
observations: Three coral dots form a simple, friendly symbol that suggests people working together.
The lowercase wordmark is soft and rounded, keeping a productivity tool feeling human.

logoResearch.name: monday.com
logoResearch.verifiedFact: monday.com is a work operating system for managing projects and workflows.
observations: Three colored marks lean forward like a progress bar or a quick checkmark.
The .com is part of the name, set lighter and smaller than the bold wordmark.

logoResearch.name: ClickUp
logoResearch.verifiedFact: ClickUp is an all-in-one productivity app for tasks, docs, and goals.
observations: The symbol is an upward chevron with a gradient, a literal nod to the name.
Bold, rounded type keeps the brand energetic and approachable.

logoResearch.name: Airtable
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Airtable is a spreadsheet-database hybrid for building apps and workflows.
observations: Three colored shapes form an isometric box, like a stack of data.
The friendly wordmark balances the more technical-looking symbol.

logoResearch.name: Miro
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Miro is an online whiteboard for team collaboration.
observations: A yellow tile holds a hand-drawn-style M, like a sticky note.
Lowercase type keeps the brand playful and creative.

logoResearch.name: Loom
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Loom is a video messaging tool, now part of Atlassian.
observations: The blue starburst symbol suggests a camera shutter and a burst of energy.
Since the acquisition, the lockup carries the Atlassian name above the product name.

logoResearch.name: Calendly
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Calendly is a scheduling tool that removes back-and-forth emails.
observations: A heavy, tight wordmark makes the long name feel compact.
The bold black type works well on booking pages where the customer's brand also appears.

logoResearch.name: Zapier
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Zapier connects thousands of apps to automate workflows.
observations: A short orange underscore before the name hints at code and connections.
The bold lowercase wordmark is simple and easy to recognize.

logoResearch.name: Grammarly
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Grammarly is an AI writing assistant.
observations: A green circle with a G that turns into an arrow suggests improvement.
The friendly lowercase wordmark matches the helpful tone of the product.

logoResearch.name: GitHub
logoResearch.verifiedFact: GitHub is the world's largest platform for hosting code, owned by Microsoft.
observations: The heavy wordmark has a playful, chunky rhythm.
The Octocat symbol is often used alongside it as a separate mark.

logoResearch.name: GitLab
logoResearch.verifiedFact: GitLab is a DevOps platform for software teams.
observations: The orange tanuki is built from simple triangles in warm shades.
A grey wordmark keeps the colorful symbol in focus.

logoResearch.name: Retool
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Retool lets companies build internal tools quickly.
observations: The symbol is built from blocky shapes, like UI components snapping together.
A clean sans-serif wordmark keeps it simple.

logoResearch.name: Snowflake
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Snowflake is a cloud data platform.
observations: A crisp, symmetrical snowflake matches the name perfectly.
Light blue reads as cool and clean, like data in the cloud.

logoResearch.name: MongoDB
logoResearch.verifiedFact: MongoDB is a popular document database.
observations: A green leaf symbolizes growth and something organic, unusual for a database.
The serif wordmark with the capital DB has a distinctive, almost editorial feel.

logoResearch.name: Supabase
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Supabase is an open-source backend platform for developers.
observations: A green lightning bolt suggests speed.
The bold lowercase wordmark feels developer-friendly.

logoResearch.name: Netlify
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Netlify is a platform for building and deploying websites.
observations: Lines radiate around the name, suggesting deployment and connection.
Teal is distinctive among developer tools.

logoResearch.name: Sentry
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Sentry is an error monitoring tool for developers.
observations: The symbol resembles a watchful eye or a peak, fitting a tool that keeps watch.
Spaced capitals give the wordmark a steady, reliable tone.

logoResearch.name: Twilio
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Twilio provides APIs for messaging, voice, and video.
observations: A red circle with four dots suggests a phone or a connection.
The bold red wordmark is strong and memorable.

logoResearch.name: HubSpot
logoResearch.verifiedFact: HubSpot makes CRM and marketing software for growing businesses.

logoResearch.name: Intercom
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Intercom is a customer messaging and support platform.

A heavy lowercase wordmark keeps it approachable.

logoResearch.name: Zendesk
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Zendesk is a customer service software company.
observations: Two shapes form a Z, balanced like yin and yang.

logoResearch.name: Mailchimp

logoResearch.name: Gong

logoResearch.name: Pipedrive

logoResearch.name: Webflow

logoResearch.name: Klaviyo

logoResearch.name: Semrush

logoResearch.name: Ramp

logoResearch.name: Brex

logoResearch.name: Gusto
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Gusto is a payroll and HR platform for small businesses.

logoResearch.name: Justworks
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Justworks is a payroll, benefits, and HR platform for small businesses.

logoResearch.name: Vanta
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Vanta automates security compliance for companies.
observations: A deep purple serif wordmark feels trustworthy and premium.
The serif is unusual for a security tool and helps it stand out.

logoResearch.name: DocuSign
logoResearch.verifiedFact: DocuSign is the leading e-signature platform.

logoResearch.name: Carta

logoResearch.name: Expensify

logoResearch.name: BILL

logoResearch.name: Cursor

logoResearch.name: Perplexity
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Perplexity is an AI-powered answer engine.

logoResearch.name: ElevenLabs

logoResearch.name: Runway

logoResearch.name: Synthesia

logoResearch.name: Glean

The g has a playful, open tail.

logoResearch.name: Gamma
logoResearch.verifiedFact: Gamma uses AI to create presentations, documents, and websites.

The minimal black treatment matches a design-focused product.

logoResearch.name: Jasper

logoResearch.name: Lovable

listIntro: The boards below show all 45 SaaS logos in one consistent format, grouped into productivity, developer tools, sales and marketing, finance and HR, and AI SaaS.
Each logo is reviewed for its design decisions, not for the product's features or pricing.
sectionIntroductions: Productivity tools live in browser tabs all day, so their logos tend to be colorful, friendly, and built around a small, memorable symbol.
Developer brands speak to engineers, so many of them use monochrome marks, technical shapes, and confident, no-nonsense type.
Sales and marketing platforms compete for attention, and their logos often use one bright, ownable color.
Finance and HR software has to feel trustworthy, so these logos lean on bold, stable wordmarks and restrained color.
AI SaaS brands are young and moving fast, and most of them choose minimal, black-and-white identities with one distinctive detail.
sectionBridge: This is a visual comparison of SaaS logos, not a ranking of software.
Look at how each logo works as a small icon in a tool stack and how much of it is symbol, color, or type.
entryFallbacks: The identity relies on a few clear decisions to stay recognizable.
Notice how the logo holds up when reduced to a favicon or integration tile.

findings.heading: A compact symbol is a SaaS superpower
findings.text: Asana, Airtable, and Webflow all have marks that work alone as favicons, app icons, and integration tiles.

findings.heading: One color can carry the brand
findings.text: HubSpot orange, Twilio red, and Supabase green are recognizable in a sidebar before you read the name.

findings.heading: Developer brands stay monochrome
findings.text: GitHub, Sentry, and Retool use black-and-white identities that feel at home in a code editor or dark mode dashboard.

findings.heading: AI SaaS is going minimal
findings.text: Cursor, Perplexity, and ElevenLabs use quiet, precise identities with one small detail instead of flashy gradients.

logoRosterConfig.checklistHeading: A practical checklist for a new SaaS logo
checklistItems: Does the symbol still read as a 16-pixel favicon and an integration tile?
Does it work in light and dark mode?
Can you own one color in your category?
Does the wordmark feel friendly to users and credible to buyers?
Will it still fit when the product grows past its first feature?
